He said Russia…
sources: President Volodymyr Zelensky, comments to journalists, reported by Interfax-Ukraine, New Voice of Ukraine and The Standard
fault_line: Should Ukraine's future be settled at a great-power table (Trump-Putin-Xi) or only with Kyiv at the table -- is a trilateral a shortcut to peace or a carve-up?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM / ATTRIBUTED REPORT] Zelensky warned that an expected Trump-Putin-Xi meeting (under preparation for the APEC sidelines, Nov 18-19 Shenzhen, per the Kremlin) must not become a redistribution of influence: 'We really don't want this to turn into Yalta 2, 3, 4.' He said Russia wants the meeting more than anyone, that what the three might discuss is not yet defined, and that Ukraine wants Abu Dhabi talks with the US and Russia BEFORE any trilateral. Separately, Zelensky said the US asked to postpone a planned Brussels meeting (Ukraine + US + EU leaders + NATO Secretary General) because US representatives need to be in Washington amid the Middle East situation; no new date proposed yet. He also urged more US Patriot interceptors.
sections.what_verified: Interfax-Ukraine (T3) for the Brussels postponement + New Voice of Ukraine and The Standard carrying the Yalta warning with direct quotes; the APEC trilateral possibility traces to WSJ Oct 18 reporting of a Putin proposal and Trump's stated openness.
sections.what_disputed: No trilateral meeting is agreed: Trump has said he has not agreed to one but will if Putin and Xi want it; no date is set for the Abu Dhabi talks either. The Yalta framing is Zelensky's warning, not a confirmed agenda -- the three leaders' discussion topics are, by his own account, undefined.
sections.why_matters: Proven-set lane (NATO/Russia war warnings): Kyiv's pre-emptive strike against being negotiated over -- lead with the Yalta line + the 12-vs-150 Patriot gap, not with meeting logistics.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Oct 28 daytime , in no prior Oct 28/29 scan as a standalone item) -- Zelensky warns against a 'Yalta 2, 3, 4' carve-up at a possible Trump-Putin-Xi meeting; US asks to postpone the Brussels Ukraine/EU/NATO meeting over Middle East demands

totw_analysis: Our read: Proven-set lane (NATO/Russia war warnings): Kyiv's pre-emptive strike against being negotiated over -- lead with the Yalta line + the 12-vs-150 Patriot gap, not with meeting logistics. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Should Ukraine's future be settled at a great-power table (Trump-Putin-Xi) or only with Kyiv at the table -- is a trilateral a shortcut to peace or a carve-up?
